title: Decouple admission throttles from scheduler; implement rapid priming and per-tenant queue caps after hosted GPU exhaustion
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Summary: During a delta of sustained high-concurrency generations (mixed short chat + long-sequence requests) hosted-api GPU pools hit an exhaustion event that caused head-of-line queue buildup, request throttling, and visible application errors for customers. This ticket tracks follow-up engineering work to prevent recurrence by separating admission control from scheduling logic, improving autoscaler priming behavior, and adding per-tenant queue caps and eviction policies.
impact: On 2026-03-08 04:20 UTC we observed GPU pool saturation across two regions; ~18% of active requests hit 502/503 during the 12 minute peak and several customers reported elevated latency/timeouts. Cost exposure: short-term spike in prewarmed capacity during recovery attempts; SLA incidents were triggered for 3 enterprise customers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Replay peak traffic trace (link below) with mix: 55% small chat (seq 64), 35% medium (seq 512), 10% long generation (seq 2048+) at 250 req/s for 15 minutes. 2) Use current admission policy + node scheduler to route to same GPU pools. 3) Observe queue growth, admission scoring favoring 'earliest enqueued' jobs and scheduler failing to pre-warm additional nodes quickly enough. 4) Confirm pipeline-level head-of-line blocking when large seq requests occupy GPU slots and prevent rapid dequeueing of short requests.
root_cause: 1) Tight coupling between admission controller and node scheduler: admission allowed high-cost long-sequence requests into queues even when scheduler had not primed capacity for long-latency workloads, creating head-of-line blocking. 2) Autoscaler priming used conservative cooldown/hysteresis which delayed bringing additional nodes online fast enough for bursty traffic. 3) No per-tenant or per-route queue caps, enabling a noisy neighbor to consume queue slots. 4) Cache warmers and KV cache priming missing for long-context models causing longer per-request GPU time.
resolution_summary: Implemented temporary mitigations: emergency rate cap on max sequence length per tenant, prioritized short requests via a lightweight fast-path admission heuristic, and manual override to prime two GPU nodes per hot pool. This reduced observed error rate to near zero for the subsequent 24h window. The long-term program below captures the permanent fixes.
action_items: Decouple admission decisions from scheduler: admission should consider only per-request cost scoring and per-tenant quotas; scheduling decisions will map admitted work onto nodes asynchronously (owner: Ravi, estimate: 3)
Fast-prime autoscaler: add a burst priming mode that can temporarily bypass conservative cooldowns and request 1-2 nodes with 'rush' priority for short windows (owner: SRE team, estimate: 5)
Per-tenant queue caps & grace eviction: implement soft caps with exponential backoff + hard reject for tenants that exceed their in-flight queue allocation (owner: Backend, estimate: 3)

Short-request fast-path: add an admission shortcut for requests under 128 tokens so they can be routed to CPU-prefill or smaller GPU slots without waiting behind large seq jobs (owner: Runtime team, estimate: 3)

KV-cache warmers & sequence-aware batching: add prewarm for known long-context workloads and batch long sequences separately to avoid degrading short-request latency (owner: Serving runtime, estimate: 5)

Observability & runbooks: add metrics for 'admission wait time by tenant', 'queue occupancy by seq-length bins', and update the capacity playbook with explicit priming run scenarios (owner: Observability, estimate: 2)
Integration tests: add a synthetic burst test to CI that simulates mixed-length bursts and validates admission + autoscaler behavior (owner: Test infra, estimate: 2)

Canary rollout plan: staged rollout of admission-scheduler decoupling behind a config flag; run in canary region for 72h with synthetic traffic and blue/green fallback (owner: Release eng, estimate: 2)
Customer communication: prepare template for impacted customers summarizing fixes and mitigation options (owner: CS/PM, estimate: 1)
Cost guardrails: add temporary budget alert for autoscaler rush-mode to avoid unbounded spend during priming windows (owner: Finance eng, estimate: 1)
